research_question: Does a Dual policy that learned the normal detour turn rare stochastic wall crossings into a beneficial shortcut after mutant adaptation?
understood_as: Branch only the two passing Dual development checkpoints into fixed continuation and mutant adaptation, keep the locked 4096-update contract, evaluate each policy in both kernels, and do not launch GC adaptation.

training.method: Dual PPO with adapting all-goal teacher and policy BC
training.bc_schedule: 0.1 at global update 0, linearly decayed to 0 at global update 4608; adaptation begins at global update 512 with coefficient 0.0888889

secondary: first wall-pass origin, action, intermediate cell, and destination
evaluation.length_guard: Do not interpret shorter mean successful length without success rate; failures are not included in mean_success_length.
evaluation.trigger_payoff_separation: A wall crossing and a delivery benefiting from a wall crossing are distinct outcomes.

home.decision: excluded for new large checkpoint run

execution.resume: Each cell resumes only from a complete retained checkpoint whose global update and config match.
execution.gpu_keepalive: Stop only the identity-checked dummy, then guard the owned runner against dummy recreation.

completion_rule: All four preregistered branches reach adaptation update 4096 and have frozen two-kernel mode and sample evaluations at every checkpoint.
followup_rule: If beneficial shortcut use appears, freeze this configuration before any independent-seed replication. Do not add map, model-size, algorithm, or budget sweeps to this development run.
interpretation_guards: These are two development seeds, not an independent replication.
GC is absent because it failed the fixed method gate; this run cannot establish Dual-versus-GC superiority on spatial wall pass.
A higher wall-pass rate without beneficial use or payoff improvement is not strong evidence of an exploit strategy.
Adaptation update 0 is a no-gradient baseline, not mutant learning.
